probe: what claude plugin eval can and cannot score, and where the measurement runner has to live
method: A throwaway plugin under /tmp with a one-case eval suite. Grader types and field names were discovered by submitting invalid values and reading the validator's own error messages. No model runs; validation only, so the cost was nil.

required_fields.regex: pattern; also accepts flags and weight. No required field beyond type

regex_negation.result: all three rejected as unrecognized keys
regex_negation.consequence: A regex grader passes when its pattern matches. 'Must not contain' has to be written as a negative lookahead inside the pattern itself.

regex_engine.question: The document claimed 'must not contain' is expressible as a negative lookahead. That assumed an engine that supports lookahead, which was never checked - a Rust regex engine would not.

probes.result: 'pattern not found in last_message' - a normal non-match, NOT a syntax error, so lookahead parses

regex_engine.finding: It is JavaScript's RegExp: lookahead is supported, inline flags like (?i) are not. So negation via negative lookahead works and the `flags` field is the way to set case-insensitivity. The document's claim was right; it had no evidence for it until now.

findings: A `regex` grader exists. Mechanical scoring inside claude plugin eval is therefore possible without the llm grader E3 disqualified - which the first reading of C3 did not know.

But it is presence-matching only. There is no negation field, so every 'must not contain' rule becomes a lookahead; density thresholds become repetition counts; and a RATIO - the share of sentences ending without EF, the share of 체언 without a particle - cannot be expressed at all.
Tier 1 (morphological) and Tier 2 (input vs output) are outside what any of the six grader types can do.
So the tool covers trigger and regression checks, and cannot carry the measurement battery.

other.bare_template: claude plugin eval init --bare writes prompt.md + graders/criteria.md with type: llm and weight: 1
other.existing_suite: tests/evals/claude-code/ uses 4 tool_used graders and 2 llm graders; the llm ones are the two policy cases C3 re-ran
other.tests_cases_runner: Verified: nothing parses tests/cases/*.yaml. No reference in build/, tests/ or build/checks.py; only design documents mention it. The 'nobody reads checks' claim holds.
